##### 1: Slippery Roof

Let me tell you a story about overcoming adversity. This is how I came to make sense of the world in a way that mattered. \

\
\*HYPERLINK "scrivcmt://26A1AC6A-9111-4691-B8D7-D38055D1FA35"So few controlled so many but I was one of another few; the clever and free. The world was run on a promise kept by a few to the many that they had no intention of keeping.\
\
The many were fed lies about how things were supposed to be; what was true and what was inconceivable. \
\
The many were hoodwinked to believe that they had magic pieces of paper in their pockets that were valuable. These paper's didn't make electricity. They didn't heal wounds on their own. The newer, plastic pieces didn't even produce flame like the old paper ones. They just shrivelled and melted. \
\
The power of these plastic pieces was what people believed them to be worth. People, like they usually do, let other people tell them what to believe. They believed that the pieces were worth enough to exchange for goods, services, and what have you. If people in power decided tomorrow that the bills were worth nothing, then that would be true. People would be left holding worthless artefacts of a foolish time, while other people held everything. That day was coming and it was closer than almost everyone thought it was. Vanilan was on the right side of the almost.\
\
It wasn't always like this. The notes used to be weighed against something of actual value. That value was gold. Why gold? Gold didn't age. It stayed shiny and didn't decompose. The earliest gold coins have been found in Asia Minor, the ancient land forming modern day Turkey, dating back 600 years before the supposed birth of Jesus. Since then, the exchange of gold (and silver which is equally indestructible) helped propel humanity to the heights it's reached today. \
\
Gold was hard to carry around everywhere, and hide in your pants too. People started writing notes that promised redemption for real gold to buyers to help ease trade and commerce. That's how the plastic notes in people's pockets started. They were IOUs for shiny bullion.\
\
However, at a certain point people thought it would be good to go a step further and detach the promise of gold in exchange. They convinced the masses that the paper would hold value simply by the promise of men in power.\
\
Much smaller promises were broken every day. Caesar promised Rome he wouldn't cross the Rubicon. Hitler promised Britain he wouldn't invade Czechoslovakia.\
\
All it would take for things to go badly was a broken promise. That's why Vanilan always promoted gold. Logic still thinks he'd slick trading currecies, but that come and go almost as fast as fashion trends. The currency of Zimbabwe has inflated BLANK percent in the last 2 years. People are using wheelbarrows to buy bread.\
\
No matter rupees, rubles, dinars dollars, they all had a tendency to come and go with regimes, wars and empires. But gold. Gold stayed the same. Gold and silver held intrinsic value that could not be changed. If gold ever disappeared, society would disappear. We could have started the whole affair with coconut shells, but there was a reason we chose gold, and a reason we would have to go back to it at one point or another. Vanilan knew that point would be soon.\
\
Once the secret society came out of the shadows, it was those who had assets of real value that would prevail. While everyone else was busy sending friend requests and clubbing downtown, Vanilan was preparing for the new world order.\
\
He currently held paper gold', online commodity purchases redeemable for physical gold on demand. The redeemable part was critical. He reckoned to at least have a year before the monetary system imploded. That was enough time for to liquidate and line his basement walls with the real stuff. While it may have appeared contradictory, he needed to work within the system to escape it.\
\
It was important not to have any distractions. He had traded in all of his game systems and peddle bike for a new office chair and investment capital. His bedroom was my office, thus saving on rent. His diet consisted of snacking on washed kale and apple slices in order to detox from processed sugar and fat. He occasionally splurged in Doritos when the munchies got to him. He liked to trade using a comfy wardrobe. That could be as simple as a hoodie with no undershirt and sweatpants. It was important to be comfortable when trading for long periods of time.\
\
He traded using a desk set up that included 3 monitors. His laptop screen was one of them, where he did most of his work. He also had a flatscreen and one of those big old cube shaped monitors from the early 2000s. That way we could see multiple things at once. He would have one screen glued to the spot prices of all his current trades: gold, silver, key currency pairs and a few companies. The cubed monitor was set up to watch the news. A good trader kept his fingers to the pulse of global events at all times.\
\
Right then it was tuned into a vacant mic on a public access livestream; awaiting the spokesman of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. He was watching the news awaiting an announcement on interest rates. If the rates were cut, it would mean more people would spend and thus less incentive to buy investments. Vanilan was sure that rates would be hiked in a turn of recent momentum. This meant that people would shift their behaviour back to saving and thus the price of gold would rise significantly. He only had $100 invested in this move, but he had to start somewhere. If things went great he could make 50% return, and then shift $150 to another opportunity. It was raining outside. There was no excuse but to hustle.\

Pushing yourself into the unknown, or being pushed like me, only nets you a sense of thrill and unsettling for so long. We as humans are remarkably inclined to get used to anything. There's stories about torture victims becoming numb to the techniques used on them. Prisoners get clocks with no hands tatted on their arms to signify their peace with living something resembling a timeless existence.\
\
It should come as no surprise that my life driving for rideshare was thrilling and made me nervous for precisely a week.\*HYPERLINK "scrivcmt://454947CF-F105-48FA-981E-7567A00539AC" It wouldn't take long for someone to get me going just as strongly.\
\
Driving for Jockey made me hip to the usual travel patterns of Rexdale residents. People lived in Rexdale, went to to work in the suburb factories, and went to York for school. Mom was in the garden when I pulled in. I told her to plant things only in the backyard but it wasn't enough real estate for all her crops. She had a third of the front yard portioned off for tomato plants. There were carrots, cabbages, and more tomatoes out back.\
\
I parked and then went for the groceries in trunk while Logic went for the open arms of Mom.\
\
"The baby tomatoes are grown up. Will you cry when they go off to college like Vanilan, Auntie?" Logic said.\
\
Mom looked at her kids with pride. \
\
"They're going to go to Humber and come home every night, like Vanilan." \
\
Mom grabbed a bag of produce from my hands and I went back the trunk for more. She left Logic to tetris the fruits into the fridge.\
\
"Hello Uncle," Logic said.\
\
The garage door was open and Dad was sitting on a beach chair in the spot where the newer Camry would sleep at night. He waved with his free hand while he held onto his Labatt Blue in the other. He was in shorts that were high enough to show off his curly thigh hair. I had the same breed in lesser volume.\
\
"Stay and have some tea," Mom said.\
\
"Have a beer," Dad called from the garage. \
\
"Later," Logic called back before he turned back to Mom holding the bag of produce and hanging out o the doorway.\
\
"Only if you make it with cardamom," Logic said. He took the first baton of milk bags while I went back for more.\
\
"That's the only way to make it," she laughed.\
\
"Come inside!" she called to Dad.\
\
A few seconds later we heard the garage door puttering shut from inside the house. Mom had only let us sit on the kitchen dining table since the days of Logic coming over to play Goldeneye. I was the first kid in our grade to have an N64. Logic's parents couldn't afford one. Mom had gone to Wal-mart at 9 before they closed to buy a 2
nd
 controller for him when he'd cried that one night. I remembered that it was snowing pretty bad that night too.\
\
"Why don't you come over more often. He's been getting into a lot of trouble recently," Mom called from the stove.\
\
I fit five out of six milk bags on the bottom shelf of the fridge. The veggies were on the counter for Mom to deal with herself but I had to get the milk in before it went bad.\
\
"I'm busy with work Auntie. I'm sorry for being a stranger. I'll try to come over more often," Logic said.\
\
They'd had the same interaction the last five odd times he'd been over. I wanted to tell Mom that things fall apart and people grow up and behaviours change and I didn't need someone to keep tabs on me, especially someone who was a drug dealer.\
\
Instead I sipped on the coke I'd poured out of the 2 litre on the bottom shelf of the fridge to make room for all the milk. It had 3 cups left in it so I poured a bit more while it was still cold.\
\
The tea was already made so Mom just had to heat it up. She didn't like putting it in the microwave so she boiled it over again really quick. My parents were from the old country so I understood why they liked the stuff. Logic was from Guyana and had moved here when he was seven so I didn't know why he liked it. He told me he actually like it and didn't just drink it to please my mom when I'd asked him one night he'd slept over.\
\
The stuff had too much sugar and milk for starters. Then it tasted like all the over-powerful spices she put into the dinner food as well. I only drank it black whenever I hadn't shit in a while and usually all of the blockage came out within a few minutes afterwards. The tea was good for inducing shits but that's about it.\
\
She poured him a steaming cup and he thanked her.\
\
"Keep an eye on him. He's gotten corrupted hanging with blacks since you left," she said.\
\
"I'll make sure he doesn't get in any more trouble Auntie."\
\
"I'll try my best," he addended.\
\
Then he sipped his tea. He made sure Mom had her head tucked into the fridge puzzling fruits and veggies when he gave me a wink from the dark side of his up-held cup. He was a bastard.

##### 12: Peel His Skin Off

I hadn't traded in a while I still had about $200 in a buy position on silver that I had let ride until it hit $20. That's the equivalaent of auto-pilot but to tell you the truth I would like cut my wrists if I was driving the day that 200 became 2000 and I wasn't at the office to inject more capital.\
\
But that was the problem: capital. I didn't have any. I drove my ass off and was buying half ounces off Logic for a better price then a dime at a time, but that just meant I smoke more. I was smoking right before picking up people and my car constantly smelled like Febreeze Auto and cheap cologne. One day I realized it smelled like a taxi when I happened to recall the time I took one home from a school visit to the AGO with our chaperone.\
\
Anyways, the weed was a problem and I had to get that under control. Besides that, I was paying mad loot for gas like twice a day and I and to take the car in for a check-up one every 14 days with a receipt to scan and sent to Jockey. Then my parents were making me pay for things that used to be free like groceries and my cell phone bill. I felt like an idiot complaining about this stuff since it's part of being a real adult but it was sucking away every dollar I had and so far I'd only been able to put away $150 for trading. I had basically sworn away trading until I had a grand to pump into a position. It was pointless sitting in front of the desk wishing on $200 bucks to turn into the cure for all that ailed me. With a few thousand I could hopefully start making enough off of minor market movements to fund myself through good trades. It was taking hella long getting the loot together though.\
\
I didn't try and talk to passengers now. I mean, if someone was in the chatty mood, I could turn it on no problem. People all liked to talk about that same things with strangers anyways; the weather, sports, the incompetency of the municipal government, celebrities, construction and the incompetence of the federal government.\
\
I wasn't getting lost as much anymore. I stuck to majot roads downtown so I knew how they each ebbed and flowed through the day. I took on any shortcuts suggested by people. I found if I suggested we just follow the GPS they would get pissy and probably give me a bad rating. People liked it when you followed their advice. IF it meant taking longer to get there, I got paid more. If it meant shorter to get there, I just grabbed another fare and was off again.\
\
I was on the corner of Finch and Islington waiting for a fare to come out of... Brar Sweets, I presumed. I heard the door open and close. There was no destination entered so this is when I ask.\
\
"Where you heading?"\
\
"Oh shit, I knew it waas you."\
\
I turned around. It was Manpreet. Manpreet from Malton. Manpreet with the lazy eye who bottled Sleepy at the grade 11 semi-formal. I hadn't noticed his name on the app. Then again, it was a name common enough around here.\
\
"Hey, how's it hanging," I said, feigning a smile. I leaned forward and held out a daps for him. He hesitated before returning it.\
\
"Everything's blessed." \
\
Dudes from Malton all talked like that. It was hella foolish.\
\
"You a taxi driver now?"\
\
Manpreet may as well have had on the same clothes on as the last time I saw him. He had sneakers that looked to had been passed between a few dog's mouths. His jeans were faded, not likely from wash, but assuredly from being dragged across a few surfaces by God knew who. His hair was gelled back but it had been a few days since application so it was crusting at the roots along his forehead.\
\
"I do this when I have free time. I'm trading now. I make cash on the side when my positions are set for the next little while. Right now I'm shorting CAD..."\
\
"I don't know what the fuck you're talking about," Manpreet said.\
\
That was enough chit-chat then. I pulled out and merged with the traffic northbound on Islington. I remembered that I didn't know where I was heading.\
\
"Where are you heading?"\
\
"Kipling," Manpreet said.\
\
That was half of the equation then.\
\
"Kipling and...?" I asked.\
\
Manpreet was thinking.\
\
"Steeles," he said.\
\
That was a generic as fuck intersection but it was busy so I went that way. We were driving for a bit before he spoke again.\
\
"Are you still hanging out with the pussy Logic?"\
\
I was caught off guard by the remark.\
\
\*HYPERLINK "scrivcmt://13C29386-19B4-4C00-BDC2-E745D78B81D2""I see him once and a while. I'm usually busy driving," I said.\
\
Manpreet was looking out window while he digested my response.\
\
"If you see him tell him I was 10 minutes behind him at the party. The boys texted me that he was there. He was 10 minutes ahead of needing fake teeth,"\
The Malton boys looked to Manpreet as a sometimes leader. He only coordinated their ruckus when he felt like it, but when he stirred awake they were liable to set cars on fire and slam jaws on concrete. They were in the maiming business, but not demonstrably in the killing business yet. He was like a hood version of Rasputin who didn't give as much of a shit.\
\
"Like I said I don't see him too much,"\
\
"But you'll tell him," Manpreet said.\
\
He was all eyes ahead now, waiting for an answer. No, he was looking at where he'd glued the answer and checking to see if it stuck.\
\
"Yeah, no doubt." \
\
I hadn't betrayed a friend, as the message would never make it make to Logic without some redaction. I had betrayed myself and bitched out. It was better than how Sleepy's face had looked, even after a summer to heal. He got that nickname afterwards because he'd nod off in class as an after effect of his concussion. Teenagers were assholes.\
\
Manpreet turned his head out the window again. I peeked on him and he looked deep in murderous thought. He snapped his head back and I thought it was because I was looking, until he spoke.\
\
"Where's he working now?" Manpreet asked.\
\
"He works at a Foot Locker. I'm not sure which one though," I replied.\
\
Logic had worked at Foot Locker last summer so I could front like I hadn't seen him since in case he called me out. \
Instead, he laughed.\
\
He laughed like it was actually funny. When he got a hold of himself again he reached into his pocket and started fiddling with something. He slumped his torso forward so it looked like he was getting ready to turn into a turtle. \
\
I gripped the wheel tighter and focused on the road. Steeles was the next light, then a 2 minute stretch West and this would be done.\
\
Manpreet's voice was cracking when he spoke again.\
\
"See that's the thing. All these motherfuckers have jobs and responsibilities and things they can't just let go off. They still have to live lives and shit. My dad owns a truck yard. I can just go work for him and it doesn't matter that I didn't finish the tenth grade. Everyone wants to go on dates and go to the temple and go get groceries. They still need to do all that, even if they have beef. When 
I 
have beef, I just have beef. I don't care about anything else and do anything else. The reason pussies like Logic should be scared is because I don't have anything better to do than to fuck their lives up, completely. I'll wake outside his house, his girlfriend's house, the temple, the school. I'll be everywhere, ready to peel his skin off."\
\
I wonder what in the fuck Logic had done to piss him off. It was likely not as big a deal to make the response warrant a bonafide peeling but that was how Manpreet saw things so that was all that mattered at this point.\
\
The stretch down Steeles didn't have much cars. Kipling was coming up soon and I wished the car had an ejectable seat.\
\
"Is the place around here?"\
\
"Yeah. Yeah it is," Manpreet said.\
\
I waited for more.\
\
"Pull over here. I'm good to walk,"\
\
I checked for headlights in the rear view and there were none, just Manpreet's head looking back. There was no shoulder here so I slowed down and pressed the hazard lights on. The car was (just barely) still moving when Manpreet opened the door. My foot slid off the brake and it rolled some more before I jerked it to a final stop.\
\
Manpreet got out and turned to walk back in the direction I'd just driven from. \
\
I waited until I had a few solid blocks between us before I phoned Logic.

##### 13: Wesley

Driving got tired. Then Jockey introduced a carpool feature and I began taking that lane more and more. People would agree to a ride with other riders who were going in the same roundabout direction they were, for a discounted fare. \
\
People were more likely to have conversations with other riders. I especially liked it when girls and guys met in my car. Invariably the guys would put some moves on and I got to see how good or bad it went. It was like watching those Youtube pick-up tutorials being put into practise. I found that girls liked guys who told jokes more than guys who told facts. I also found that guys who asked for numbers got shut down more often than guys who asked for Facebook. I kept notes of the best dudes and how they got results. I also liked picking up people going to parties. They were happy and outgoing and ready to make a splash. I fed off their energy. I wasn't excited about picking up people leaving parties though. They were either disappointed from getting rejected or from how many people hit on them. If things went well they were too busy making out in the back and making things hella awkward for me.\
\
One night I had picked up a very sweet couple from dinner at a bougie restaurant on Queen West. They were very polite and asked me questions. They didn't suck each other's face, but sneak a kiss here and there. They had an arm each intertwined with the other's. That was the first time I acknowledged in my mind that I'd seen a dude with a real girlfriend up close. I made a point to remember how they were. They might have been in love. It was the first time I could remember actually thinking about love in a serious way. I had been disgusted at it until I was about 12 and then I had scoffed at it as something for suckers. If there was a brand of love close to what I saw these two having I might consider it. Having a girlfriend looked nice.\
\
The couple scooted to the left and closer into each other when I picked at a white collared shirted dude from Promenade. He spilled in and apologized when a hand caught the girl's skirt. I looked back to see that this dude had lipstick kiss marks on each of his cheeks. \
\
"Are those stamps?" asked the man in the couple. His name was Colin I think.\
\
"Nope. 100% certified kisses from hot babes is more like it," he said.\
\
He had a way of saying it that made the couple laugh. The girl unburrowed from her boyfriend a little bit. I figured it was kosher to drive on. Everyone was headed towards Scarborough, on their way home.\
\
I had room for one more upfront. I told everyone I had a taker and turned off King to a U of T lecture house. I liked this part of town for the old building that the rest of the city lacked. I made sure to stress it's prettiness to tourists when solicited.\
\
A blonde girl in jeggings tucked into her socks went for the back door but saw it was full. She settled to sit beside me.\
\
"Hello." She beamed. Her voice was British or from one of the other accented English countries.\
\
"Oh, a foreigner," lipstick man said.\
\
"Are you going to get me deported?" \
\
She took it well.\
\
"No, no. I love it when I get to show off Canadian hospitality to own friends from down under,"\
\
"Well, I'm British, but you're too kind either way,"\
\
The couple laughed 
at 
the lipsticked man this time. He took it just as well.\
\
"Fair is fair. I guessed wrong. I've gone from suave, lip-kissed stud to generalizing brute. I'm Wesley by the way guys." \
\
He addressed everyone in the car and waved with both hands for a more efficient splay. \
\
"Hi Wesley." Colin started the words slowly and we all caught on to address him in unison by the end.\
\
Wesley asked us all for our names, making it clear the girl would be last. Her name was Charlote.\
\
"Well, Charlote, I'm awfully sorry for my blunt demeanour. I've just gone through a tough divorce and I'm trying to get my swing back. Talking to exotic strangers is a surefire way to dive in."\
\
Colin's girl issued an "Aw." I hadn't caught her name.\
\
He looked older now that he'd shown that piece of himself.\
\
"I'm sorry to hear that, it must be tough," Charlote said.\
\
"Yeah it's been a shit show. It's made worse because I'm currently sleeping on her couch."\
\
The rest of us laughed.\
"Why is that?" I asked.\
\
He turned to me.\
\
"Rent is expensive here bud. You should know. I loved her, and she milked my teets for every nickle. She's letting me sleep there so she doesn't look bad when people we know see me begging for replacement nickles on Ellesmere."\
\
"Jeez," was all I had. No one else chimed in either.\
\
Wesley turned his gaze back to the back of Charlote's head.\
\
"You're headed the wrong way if you're looking for a party."\
\
We'd just crossed the Don River. A rather abrupt change that signalled the end of Downtown proper.\
\
Charlote looked back and thought a bit before obliging to explain herself to a stranger.\
\
"I'm heading to a friend's party," she said.\
\
"Oh, right on. Nice to see you've got friends here already. It's a great town so you should be alright."\
\
"Yeah I've been here for two semesters now and I've definitely fallen in love with the city." \
\
She declared it to the whole group. I nodded my approval.\
\
"That's just wonderful. But I'd like to make a proposal. No one's truly seen this city until they've gotten Wesley's guided tour of the prettier bits. Would you be opposed to giving me your number and arranging a 2 hour walking tour ending in a nice ice cream."\
\
He was roundabout about it but all of us paused to hear her answer to his asking her out on a date.\
\
When she spoke words familiar to me hearing vicariously perviously came out. She said it was a nice offer but that she didn't take the number of strangers. She was quite nice about it relatively speaking. Wesley was also quite gracious of his rejection but he shut up rather suddenly afterwards. The ride was really quiet after that. I dropped off the couple at their home first. Wesley's home was next but he kindly offered to let Charlote out first so at not to be late for her party. I thought he might have been pulling a fast one to stalk her but he was rather chill about it. He moved into the front seat after she exited and walked a bit away.\
\
Then Wesley asked if I wanted to smoke with him. I considered it before agreeing. I cancelled the trip and officially punched out of being a responsible employee. \
\
Wesley pulled out some cultured strain of Orange Succubus that was new and nearly legal as he claimed. It was a mellow burning smoke that tickled a bit as it went down.\
\
We were halfway down the spliff when Wesley dropped a bomb.\
\
"I'm not really divorced. I just say that to chicks to disarm them."\
\
He said it like he was a karate instructor. I pictured him in a shiny suit snatching women's purses.\
\
"Are you fucking serious?"\
\
I sounded upset when I meant to sound more incredulous.\
\
"Yeah. It makes for a good laugh, doesn't it?"\
\
"But you lied to all of us about something that made you look like a loser,"\
\
"Yeah, but I was being a certain person. If I lied to you and told you I was a surgeon, you might still believe me, but you would see me as a different person. I was being the person I wanted to be in front of you guys. Charlote be damned. There'll be others."\
\
"Are you an actor or something?"\
\
I thought I was smarter than that question, but I guess I wasn't.\
\
He scoffed at the insinuation, before reconsidering my words.\
\
"I'm acting, sure. That's the action, but it's not the motive. I never let women know who I really am. You don't even know who I really am either. I mean, I'm Wesley, for sure. That's the name on my birth certificate, popped outta my momma on April 13
th
 at North York General. But you, or anyone else is never going to know who I really am, in a complete sense. I'm a truer me to you than I was to her, but I am not being me, for real. Do you follow?"\
\
I took a deep breath in and out. He could see he might be losing me. \
\
"You know who you are. If you let someone else know who you are, they own you. Your mother and maybe your father own you up until you start going out and doing stuff on your own. Your shrink may own you if you spill eveything to them. The cops own you if you confess things to them. Your girlfriend owns you if you spill too much over pillow talk. Make sure you're the only person who knows who you are in your totality, otherwise you're opening yourself up to become someone else's commodity."\
\
I was following him now. \
\
I was also really fucking high.

##### 15: Drunk Date

To confide, this was my first ever date. I had taken Simran out for pizza at the strip mall in 10
th
 grade but we had run into a bunch of her friends and it wasn't a date anymore. Back in those days, agreeing to get pizza was a big deal. In that dating world it was nothing to meet someone for drinks, but I still thought it was a big step due to lacking experience. \
\
This was going to be me picking up a girl and going to a bar. This was the real deal.\
\
Mariah had agreed to meet me after, like 5 sentences. I had no barometer so I could either think this was the norm, or hella sketchy. I hadn't made up my mind yet when I pulled into the Orps bumping some Sade out the speakers.\
\
I dialed her number. She said she was having a piss and would be a second.\
\
She came downstairs wearing jeans, running shoes and a hoodie. She had a big purse with her too. I stealthily untucked my dress shirt as she walked over. I also undid the collar button which had been cutting off my blood circulation. I had a fat neck that was awkward fitting in off-the-rack button ups.\
\
Her purse clinked as she sat down.\
\
"Hey hun." Her breath like mouthwash but in a freshly rinsed way.\
\
"Hey, thanks for coming out. You look good," I said.\
\
"Thanks. Bar, right?"\
\
"I was thinking we could go to a nice small bar downtown," I said.\
\
I had googled a few craft bars that would look good on a first date. I hadn't been to any of them but I'd picked up and dropped off people to most of them.\
\
"That's far. Let's go to Sharks."\
\

Sharks, so be it. I might get some cred for showing up with a girl if people remember my face.
\
\
"You bought a new purse?" It was actually better defined as a duffel bag on close inspection.\
\
"It's a bag I had lying around," she said.\
\
"Oh, lucky. How's life in the city treating you?"\
\
"My life is fucked up to be honest. I have a little kid at home and rent is hard to come by," she said.\
\
It was tough to make any more conversation on the way to Shark's. She was such a fucking buzzkill.\
\
The waitress, a different one from the one that rejected Logic, seated us at a two seat table by the glass window wall showcasing the defunct patio. They had been renovating it since early spring with little improvement.\
\
"Are you going to buy me drinks?" she said.\
\
I was taken a back.\
\
"Ugh, sure. What'll you have?"\
\
"Beers are good," she said.\
\
I ordered her a nice premium beer and coke for myself.\
\
"You don't drink?" she looked surprised.\
\
"I'm driving. I only drink when I don't have any responsibilites." I said.\
\
"You can have a couple of beers and still be good to drive," she said.\
\
"I don't risk that stuff," I said.\
\
She didn't seem to have a stake to press any further and I was glad.\
\
"I can still have fun though," I said.\
\
Her beer came. When the waitress put it down she picked it up and gulped it down in a few seconds.\
\
"Order us a few more," she said.\
\
I was fucking flabbergasted at this chick. I was clearly into a fucking shit show at this point. I could connect a few grade-school exercise book dots at this point and needed to put a foot down somewhere.\
\
"I'm going to buy you one more beer. That's it. After that you can buy your own," I said. I used an index finger to punctuate every other word. I realized I may have been being a bit too forceful and supplemented an "Alright?" with a scaffolded smile.\
\
It didn't help soften the blow much.\
\
"We're on a date. You're supposed to buy me beers," she responded.\
"I'm not your wallet. You're also supposed to talk on dates but you don't seem to want to talk about anything except booze."\
\
"I'm sorry. My heads just hurting. I got robbed today remember? I need to relax a bit."\
\
It was tough on my eyes to keep looking at her so I looked around the bar instead.\
\
I met the gaze of the biggest barman standing arms crossed by the men's washroom. His eyes were softer than I'd ever seen them, but then again we had never made eye contact before. He looked at me like he felt sorry for me. What did he know?\
\
"Yeah no worries. I get it," She looked really beat up by forces other than other people's hands.\
\
Her second beer came and she ordered 2 shots that she made clear to say would be on her tab. That bought some good will with me. She could be reasoned with. I then took the good will and tacked an exponent onto it.\
\
"I have some beers at home. About eight or so. We could hang there," I said.\
\
Don't judge me. I was horny and she was a real women. I had a mind to steer the evening somewhere interesting.\
\
"It is really eight beers? Did you count them?" She was practically salivating.\
\
Holy fuck. She was an alcoholic or something. I instantly rethought the advance. She was probably one step worse from sneaking a homeless guy in to give him roti.\
"I think my dad may have drank them though."\
\
"Your Dad drinks? He probably has a stash of Crown jugs somewhere. I know you brown guys like your Crown. Have you seen where he keeps it? Do you drink Crown?"\
\
"I don't drink a lot. I'm ready to leave actually," I said.\
\
"What? Are you going to leave me here?"\
\
"No. I brought you all the way here so I'm not going to leave you stranded. I'll take you home but only if you stop drinking and leave now." I sounded like somebody's mom.\
\
She agreed. Along the way she asked if we could stop and get some fresh air for a minute. It was one of those summer nights when the heat didn't die with the sun but the night breeze kept things in an alternating state of warm and cool almost akin to a natural body massage. I parked in behind a middle school.\
\
I got out and took my shoes off.\
\
"It's actually good to walk in grass barefoot. It's an old Tamil health trick. Natural therapy."\
\
Mariah came outside and leaned against the front hood. She brought her duffel bag out with her and pulled a litre bottle of whiskey out of it.\
\
"What the fuck," I said.\
\
She didn't bother to explain and poured a disposable plastic cup full of liquor.\
\
"You're a fucking alcoholic," I said.\
\
"You think I don't fucking know that? Everyone tells me that. Well, you all can fuck off. I know what I need and I know how to take care of myself." She took another swig.\
\
"You've been asking me to buy you drinks all night. It's obvious your dependant. But forget about me, you're dependant on booze and it'll ruin your life."\
\
"What the fuck do you know? You're some young punk who wants my pussy. You were happy to buy me stuff when you though we could fuck. Now I guess you'll have to jerk yourself off again" she was spitting while she spoke.\
\
I tried to speak but she decided she wasn't done.\
\
"Other dudes want to hang out with me. You're not the only one. I could get on my phone and have five other dude's over here like it's nothing."\
\
And then she started crying.\
\
"You don't know how tough it is. My life is fucked. I don't work. My last two boyfriends left me and cheated on me. My parents disowned me. My last boyfriend beat me. You seemed different."\
\
She couldn't lie to save herself from a loaded, pointed gun. I wasn't buying any of it.\
\
I was looking for a way out and away. I remembered where we were in relation to everything. She was only few blocks from home. She'd be OK.\
\
"I'm leaving." I went for the car. She went for the passenger side but I told her she wasn't coming along.\
\
She put her duffel in the ground and started fiddling with her phone while I pressed the ignition. I still had the window open from the drive over. Mariah bent in to the car through the one that used to be hers.\
\
"Look," she turned her phone screen towards me. It was cracked square down the middle.\
\
"This guy wants to pick me up and hang out," she said.\
\
"Then call him over."\
\
I slammed the door shut and peeled out of there. She forgot her smokes in the bucket of the passenger seats. I chucked them out the window at the first red light.

"It's a jar of pickles," I said.\
\
"Do it."\
\
I did it.\
\
"Show me some teeth too," Logic said.\
\
I smiled.\
\
He took a pic on my phone with the flash on. I turned around to see if anyone was around. A dread head was stocking up on mustard, unperturbed.\
\
I checked the paper grocery list my Mom had written on the back of a junk mail envelope. Milk was next.\
\
"This'll show chicks that you can goof of. You can even keep up one of your serious guys picks no, just put this one first in the order," Logic said.\
\
"Should I keep the one of us at Bowlerama?"\
\
I pulled out ahead of him towards the freezers.\
\
"Yeah you should. It shows you have friends and that was a good call," Logic said. His head was back in my phone again.\
\
"Why do you always text girls the same message?"\
\
We used to drink 3.5 percent until I'd convinced my parents to switch to 2%. That idea had come from my gym teacher and I'd adhered in a rarer moment of choosing the less fatty option. It was probably propelled by the fact that my parents drawn the lionshare of milk with their tea. I never liked tea. When I was younger there was never a need to stay up longer then I felt, and thus never a need for caffeine. Now I got buy with Coke, and Red Bull when yawns breached the doors of my lips.\
\
"Here, we need 6," I said as I picked the first 2 bags of milk out of the freezer.\
\
Logic grabbed two bags.\
\
"I guess it lets me keep things impersonal so I don't get my ego hurt," I said.\
\
He stopped helping and looked at me cross.\
\
"That's hella insightful. You're also hella lazy my dude. Mention something in their bio. Comment on their photos. Right now you're basically the dude who says what's up across the street when she's walking by a construction site."\
\
"Alright I'll take more time to respond. I'm not getting matches like the first week anyway. I think they have an algorithm that makes matches less frequent as you go and then you start feinding for them and end up paying for the premium app in the hopes of being validated again. That's everything I need,"\
\
Logic walked ahead for the checkout.\
\
"Man, I don't know about all that. Just don't buy the full app. That's for suckers who can't get any play on their own. You shouldn't even want to be on there long enough each day to need the full app,"\
\
I was still counting the items when Logic tugged my cart into the express check-out line.\
\
Logic helped me load up the trunk, while I started the car. I lived five blocks away.\
\
"OK, I'm reading this convo where you mention you, and I quote, am always game for a little mingling and boozing." Who talks like that?"\
\
I laughed the laugh you laugh when you don't have an answer and want to curl into yourself and kill yourself.\
\
Logic picked up on it.\
\
"Man, talk like yourself. You're cool enough that I want to hand out with you. I mean you, like how you really are," he said.\
\
"But you lie all the time."\
\
"That's because I can lie better and make up things that actually sounds cool. And how do you know this is how I really am? I may just act like this so I can get along with you. Matterfact that 
is 
 true to an extent. I'm not sure you can be a cooler, different someone. That's a fucking skill dawg. So my advice is to just be a more filtered version of the you that I like hanging out with. Leave the jedi mind tricks to the real pimps," Logic said.\
\
Mom was in the garden when I pulled in. I told her to plant things only in the backyard but it wasn't enough real estate for all her crops. She had a third of the front yard portioned off for tomato plants. There were carrots, cabbages, and more tomatoes out back.\
\
I parked and then went for the groceries in trunk while Logic went for the open arms of Mom.\
\
"The baby tomatoes are grown up. Will you cry when they go off to college like Vanilan, Auntie?" Logic said.\
\
Mom looked at her kids with pride. \
\
"They're going to go to Humber and come home every night, like Vanilan." \
\
Mom grabbed a bag of produce from my hands and I went back the trunk for more. She left Logic to tetris the fruits into the fridge.\
\
"Hello Uncle," Logic said.\
\
The garage door was open and Dad was sitting on a beach chair in the spot where the newer Camry would sleep at night. He waved with his free hand while he held onto his Labatt Blue in the other. He was in shorts that were high enough to show off his curly thigh hair. I had the same breed in lesser volume.\
\
"Stay and have some tea," Mom said.\
\
"Have a beer," Dad called from the garage. \
\
"Later," Logic called back before he turned back to Mom holding the bag of produce and hanging out o the doorway.\
\
"Only if you make it with cardamom," Logic said. He took the first baton of milk bags while I went back for more.\
\
"That's the only way to make it," she laughed.\
\
"Come inside!" she called to Dad.\
\
A few seconds later we heard the garage door puttering shut from inside the house. Mom had only let us sit on the kitchen dining table since the days of Logic coming over to play Goldeneye. I was the first kid in our grade to have an N64. Logic's parents couldn't afford one. Mom had gone to Wal-mart at 9 before they closed to buy a 2
nd
 controller for him when he'd cried that one night. I remembered that it was snowing pretty bad that night too.\
\
"Why don't you come over more often. He's been getting into a lot of trouble recently," Mom called from the stove.\
\
I fit five out of six milk bags on the bottom shelf of the fridge. The veggies were on the counter for Mom to deal with herself but I had to get the milk in before it went bad.\
\
"I'm busy with work Auntie. I'm sorry for being a stranger. I'll try to come over more often," Logic said.\
\
They'd had the same interaction the last five odd times he'd been over. I wanted to tell Mom that things fall apart and people grow up and behaviours change and I didn't need someone to keep tabs on me, especially someone who was a drug dealer.\
\
Instead I sipped on the coke I'd poured out of the 2 litre on the bottom shelf of the fridge to make room for all the milk. It had 3 cups left in it so I poured a bit more while it was still cold.\
\
The tea was already made so Mom just had to heat it up. She didn't like putting it in the microwave so she boiled it over again really quick. My parents were from the old country so I understood why they liked the stuff. Logic was from Guyana and had moved here when he was seven so I didn't know why he liked it. He told me he actually like it and didn't just drink it to please my mom when I'd asked him one night he'd slept over.\
\
The stuff had too much sugar and milk for starters. Then it tasted like all the over-powerful spices she put into the dinner food as well. I only drank it black whenever I hadn't shit in a while and usually all of the blockage came out within a few minutes afterwards. The tea was good for inducing shits but that's about it.\
\
She poured him a steaming cup and he thanked her.\
\
"Keep an eye on him. He's gotten corrupted hanging with blacks since you left," she said.\
\
"I'll make sure he doesn't get in any more trouble Auntie."\
\
"I'll try my best," he addended.\
\
Then he sipped his tea. He made sure Mom had her head tucked into the fridge puzzling fruits and veggies when he gave me a wink from the dark side of his up-held cup. He was a bastard.

###### 12: Peel His Skin Off

I hadn't traded in a while I still had about $200 in a buy position on silver that I had let ride until it hit $20. That's the equivalaent of auto-pilot but to tell you the truth I would like cut my wrists if I was driving the day that 200 became 2000 and I wasn't at the office to inject more capital.\
\
But that was the problem: capital. I didn't have any. I drove my ass off and was buying half ounces off Logic for a better price then a dime at a time, but that just meant I smoke more. I was smoking right before picking up people and my car constantly smelled like Febreeze Auto and cheap cologne. One day I realized it smelled like a taxi when I happened to recall the time I took one home from a school visit to the AGO with our chaperone.\
\
Anyways, the weed was a problem and I had to get that under control. Besides that, I was paying mad loot for gas like twice a day and I and to take the car in for a check-up one every 14 days with a receipt to scan and sent to Jockey. Then my parents were making me pay for things that used to be free like groceries and my cell phone bill. I felt like an idiot complaining about this stuff since it's part of being a real adult but it was sucking away every dollar I had and so far I'd only been able to put away $150 for trading. I had basically sworn away trading until I had a grand to pump into a position. It was pointless sitting in front of the desk wishing on $200 bucks to turn into the cure for all that ailed me. With a few thousand I could hopefully start making enough off of minor market movements to fund myself through good trades. It was taking hella long getting the loot together though.\
\
I didn't try and talk to passengers now. I mean, if someone was in the chatty mood, I could turn it on no problem. People all liked to talk about that same things with strangers anyways; the weather, sports, the incompetency of the municipal government, celebrities, construction and the incompetence of the federal government.\
\
I wasn't getting lost as much anymore. I stuck to majot roads downtown so I knew how they each ebbed and flowed through the day. I took on any shortcuts suggested by people. I found if I suggested we just follow the GPS they would get pissy and probably give me a bad rating. People liked it when you followed their advice. IF it meant taking longer to get there, I got paid more. If it meant shorter to get there, I just grabbed another fare and was off again.\
\
I was on the corner of Finch and Islington waiting for a fare to come out of... Brar Sweets, I presumed. I heard the door open and close. There was no destination entered so this is when I ask.\
\
"Where you heading?"\
\
"Oh shit, I knew it waas you."\
\
I turned around. It was Manpreet. Manpreet from Malton. Manpreet with the lazy eye who bottled Sleepy at the grade 11 semi-formal. I hadn't noticed his name on the app. Then again, it was a name common enough around here.\
\
"Hey, how's it hanging," I said, feigning a smile. I leaned forward and held out a daps for him. He hesitated before returning it.\
\
"Everything's blessed." \
\
Dudes from Malton all talked like that. It was hella foolish.\
\
"You a taxi driver now?"\
\
Manpreet may as well have had on the same clothes on as the last time I saw him. He had sneakers that looked to had been passed between a few dog's mouths. His jeans were faded, not likely from wash, but assuredly from being dragged across a few surfaces by God knew who. His hair was gelled back but it had been a few days since application so it was crusting at the roots along his forehead.\
\
"I do this when I have free time. I'm trading now. I make cash on the side when my positions are set for the next little while. Right now I'm shorting CAD..."\
\
"I don't know what the fuck you're talking about," Manpreet said.\
\
That was enough chit-chat then. I pulled out and merged with the traffic northbound on Islington. I remembered that I didn't know where I was heading.\
\
"Where are you heading?"\
\
"Kipling," Manpreet said.\
\
That was half of the equation then.\
\
"Kipling and...?" I asked.\
\
Manpreet was thinking.\
\
"Steeles," he said.\
\
That was a generic as fuck intersection but it was busy so I went that way. We were driving for a bit before he spoke again.\
\
"Are you still hanging out with the pussy Logic?"\
\
I was caught off guard by the remark.\
\
\*HYPERLINK "scrivcmt://13C29386-19B4-4C00-BDC2-E745D78B81D2""I see him once and a while. I'm usually busy driving," I said.\
\
Manpreet was looking out window while he digested my response.\
\
"If you see him tell him I was 10 minutes behind him at the party. The boys texted me that he was there. He was 10 minutes ahead of needing fake teeth,"\
The Malton boys looked to Manpreet as a sometimes leader. He only coordinated their ruckus when he felt like it, but when he stirred awake they were liable to set cars on fire and slam jaws on concrete. They were in the maiming business, but not demonstrably in the killing business yet. He was like a hood version of Rasputin who didn't give as much of a shit.\
\
"Like I said I don't see him too much,"\
\
"But you'll tell him," Manpreet said.\
\
He was all eyes ahead now, waiting for an answer. No, he was looking at where he'd glued the answer and checking to see if it stuck.\
\
"Yeah, no doubt." \
\
I hadn't betrayed a friend, as the message would never make it make to Logic without some redaction. I had betrayed myself and bitched out. It was better than how Sleepy's face had looked, even after a summer to heal. He got that nickname afterwards because he'd nod off in class as an after effect of his concussion. Teenagers were assholes.\
\
Manpreet turned his head out the window again. I peeked on him and he looked deep in murderous thought. He snapped his head back and I thought it was because I was looking, until he spoke.\
\
"Where's he working now?" Manpreet asked.\
\
"He works at a Foot Locker. I'm not sure which one though," I replied.\
\
Logic had worked at Foot Locker last summer so I could front like I hadn't seen him since in case he called me out. \
Instead, he laughed.\
\
He laughed like it was actually funny. When he got a hold of himself again he reached into his pocket and started fiddling with something. He slumped his torso forward so it looked like he was getting ready to turn into a turtle. \
\
I gripped the wheel tighter and focused on the road. Steeles was the next light, then a 2 minute stretch West and this would be done.\
\
Manpreet's voice was cracking when he spoke again.\
\
"See that's the thing. All these motherfuckers have jobs and responsibilities and things they can't just let go off. They still have to live lives and shit. My dad owns a truck yard. I can just go work for him and it doesn't matter that I didn't finish the tenth grade. Everyone wants to go on dates and go to the temple and go get groceries. They still need to do all that, even if they have beef. When 
I 
have beef, I just have beef. I don't care about anything else and do anything else. The reason pussies like Logic should be scared is because I don't have anything better to do than to fuck their lives up, completely. I'll wake outside his house, his girlfriend's house, the temple, the school. I'll be everywhere, ready to peel his skin off."\
\
I wonder what in the fuck Logic had done to piss him off. It was likely not as big a deal to make the response warrant a bonafide peeling but that was how Manpreet saw things so that was all that mattered at this point.\
\
The stretch down Steeles didn't have much cars. Kipling was coming up soon and I wished the car had an ejectable seat.\
\
"Is the place around here?"\
\
"Yeah. Yeah it is," Manpreet said.\
\
I waited for more.\
\
"Pull over here. I'm good to walk,"\
\
I checked for headlights in the rear view and there were none, just Manpreet's head looking back. There was no shoulder here so I slowed down and pressed the hazard lights on. The car was (just barely) still moving when Manpreet opened the door. My foot slid off the brake and it rolled some more before I jerked it to a final stop.\
\
Manpreet got out and turned to walk back in the direction I'd just driven from. \
\
I waited until I had a few solid blocks between us before I phoned Logic.

###### 13: Wesley

Driving got tired. Then Jockey introduced a carpool feature and I began taking that lane more and more. People would agree to a ride with other riders who were going in the same roundabout direction they were, for a discounted fare. \
\
People were more likely to have conversations with other riders. I especially liked it when girls and guys met in my car. Invariably the guys would put some moves on and I got to see how good or bad it went. It was like watching those Youtube pick-up tutorials being put into practise. I found that girls liked guys who told jokes more than guys who told facts. I also found that guys who asked for numbers got shut down more often than guys who asked for Facebook. I kept notes of the best dudes and how they got results. I also liked picking up people going to parties. They were happy and outgoing and ready to make a splash. I fed off their energy. I wasn't excited about picking up people leaving parties though. They were either disappointed from getting rejected or from how many people hit on them. If things went well they were too busy making out in the back and making things hella awkward for me.\
\
One night I had picked up a very sweet couple from dinner at a bougie restaurant on Queen West. They were very polite and asked me questions. They didn't suck each other's face, but sneak a kiss here and there. They had an arm each intertwined with the other's. That was the first time I acknowledged in my mind that I'd seen a dude with a real girlfriend up close. I made a point to remember how they were. They might have been in love. It was the first time I could remember actually thinking about love in a serious way. I had been disgusted at it until I was about 12 and then I had scoffed at it as something for suckers. If there was a brand of love close to what I saw these two having I might consider it. Having a girlfriend looked nice.\
\
The couple scooted to the left and closer into each other when I picked at a white collared shirted dude from Promenade. He spilled in and apologized when a hand caught the girl's skirt. I looked back to see that this dude had lipstick kiss marks on each of his cheeks. \
\
"Are those stamps?" asked the man in the couple. His name was Colin I think.\
\
"Nope. 100% certified kisses from hot babes is more like it," he said.\
\
He had a way of saying it that made the couple laugh. The girl unburrowed from her boyfriend a little bit. I figured it was kosher to drive on. Everyone was headed towards Scarborough, on their way home.\
\
I had room for one more upfront. I told everyone I had a taker and turned off King to a U of T lecture house. I liked this part of town for the old building that the rest of the city lacked. I made sure to stress it's prettiness to tourists when solicited.\
\
A blonde girl in jeggings tucked into her socks went for the back door but saw it was full. She settled to sit beside me.\
\
"Hello." She beamed. Her voice was British or from one of the other accented English countries.\
\
"Oh, a foreigner," lipstick man said.\
\
"Are you going to get me deported?" \
\
She took it well.\
\
"No, no. I love it when I get to show off Canadian hospitality to own friends from down under,"\
\
"Well, I'm British, but you're too kind either way,"\
\
The couple laughed 
at 
the lipsticked man this time. He took it just as well.\
\
"Fair is fair. I guessed wrong. I've gone from suave, lip-kissed stud to generalizing brute. I'm Wesley by the way guys." \
\
He addressed everyone in the car and waved with both hands for a more efficient splay. \
\
"Hi Wesley." Colin started the words slowly and we all caught on to address him in unison by the end.\
\
Wesley asked us all for our names, making it clear the girl would be last. Her name was Charlote.\
\
"Well, Charlote, I'm awfully sorry for my blunt demeanour. I've just gone through a tough divorce and I'm trying to get my swing back. Talking to exotic strangers is a surefire way to dive in."\
\
Colin's girl issued an "Aw." I hadn't caught her name.\
\
He looked older now that he'd shown that piece of himself.\
\
"I'm sorry to hear that, it must be tough," Charlote said.\
\
"Yeah it's been a shit show. It's made worse because I'm currently sleeping on her couch."\
\
The rest of us laughed.\
"Why is that?" I asked.\
\
He turned to me.\
\
"Rent is expensive here bud. You should know. I loved her, and she milked my teets for every nickle. She's letting me sleep there so she doesn't look bad when people we know see me begging for replacement nickles on Ellesmere."\
\
"Jeez," was all I had. No one else chimed in either.\
\
Wesley turned his gaze back to the back of Charlote's head.\
\
"You're headed the wrong way if you're looking for a party."\
\
We'd just crossed the Don River. A rather abrupt change that signalled the end of Downtown proper.\
\
Charlote looked back and thought a bit before obliging to explain herself to a stranger.\
\
"I'm heading to a friend's party," she said.\
\
"Oh, right on. Nice to see you've got friends here already. It's a great town so you should be alright."\
\
"Yeah I've been here for two semesters now and I've definitely fallen in love with the city." \
\
She declared it to the whole group. I nodded my approval.\
\
"That's just wonderful. But I'd like to make a proposal. No one's truly seen this city until they've gotten Wesley's guided tour of the prettier bits. Would you be opposed to giving me your number and arranging a 2 hour walking tour ending in a nice ice cream."\
\
He was roundabout about it but all of us paused to hear her answer to his asking her out on a date.\
\
When she spoke words familiar to me hearing vicariously perviously came out. She said it was a nice offer but that she didn't take the number of strangers. She was quite nice about it relatively speaking. Wesley was also quite gracious of his rejection but he shut up rather suddenly afterwards. The ride was really quiet after that. I dropped off the couple at their home first. Wesley's home was next but he kindly offered to let Charlote out first so at not to be late for her party. I thought he might have been pulling a fast one to stalk her but he was rather chill about it. He moved into the front seat after she exited and walked a bit away.\
\
Then Wesley asked if I wanted to smoke with him. I considered it before agreeing. I cancelled the trip and officially punched out of being a responsible employee. \
\
Wesley pulled out some cultured strain of Orange Succubus that was new and nearly legal as he claimed. It was a mellow burning smoke that tickled a bit as it went down.\
\
We were halfway down the spliff when Wesley dropped a bomb.\
\
"I'm not really divorced. I just say that to chicks to disarm them."\
\
He said it like he was a karate instructor. I pictured him in a shiny suit snatching women's purses.\
\
"Are you fucking serious?"\
\
I sounded upset when I meant to sound more incredulous.\
\
"Yeah. It makes for a good laugh, doesn't it?"\
\
"But you lied to all of us about something that made you look like a loser,"\
\
"Yeah, but I was being a certain person. If I lied to you and told you I was a surgeon, you might still believe me, but you would see me as a different person. I was being the person I wanted to be in front of you guys. Charlote be damned. There'll be others."\
\
"Are you an actor or something?"\
\
I thought I was smarter than that question, but I guess I wasn't.\
\
He scoffed at the insinuation, before reconsidering my words.\
\
"I'm acting, sure. That's the action, but it's not the motive. I never let women know who I really am. You don't even know who I really am either. I mean, I'm Wesley, for sure. That's the name on my birth certificate, popped outta my momma on April 13
th
 at North York General. But you, or anyone else is never going to know who I really am, in a complete sense. I'm a truer me to you than I was to her, but I am not being me, for real. Do you follow?"\
\
I took a deep breath in and out. He could see he might be losing me. \
\
"You know who you are. If you let someone else know who you are, they own you. Your mother and maybe your father own you up until you start going out and doing stuff on your own. Your shrink may own you if you spill eveything to them. The cops own you if you confess things to them. Your girlfriend owns you if you spill too much over pillow talk. Make sure you're the only person who knows who you are in your totality, otherwise you're opening yourself up to become someone else's commodity."\
\
I was following him now. \
\
I was also really fucking high.

###### 15: Drunk Date

To confide, this was my first ever date. I had taken Simran out for pizza at the strip mall in 10
th
 grade but we had run into a bunch of her friends and it wasn't a date anymore. Back in those days, agreeing to get pizza was a big deal. In that dating world it was nothing to meet someone for drinks, but I still thought it was a big step due to lacking experience. \
\
This was going to be me picking up a girl and going to a bar. This was the real deal.\
\
Mariah had agreed to meet me after, like 5 sentences. I had no barometer so I could either think this was the norm, or hella sketchy. I hadn't made up my mind yet when I pulled into the Orps bumping some Sade out the speakers.\
\
I dialed her number. She said she was having a piss and would be a second.\
\
She came downstairs wearing jeans, running shoes and a hoodie. She had a big purse with her too. I stealthily untucked my dress shirt as she walked over. I also undid the collar button which had been cutting off my blood circulation. I had a fat neck that was awkward fitting in off-the-rack button ups.\
\
Her purse clinked as she sat down.\
\
"Hey hun." Her breath like mouthwash but in a freshly rinsed way.\
\

"That's far. Let's go to Sharks."\

I was taken a back.\

Her beer came. When the waitress put it down she picked it up and gulped it down in a few seconds.\

"I'm not your wallet. You're also supposed to talk on dates but you don't seem to want to talk about anything except booze."\

It was tough on my eyes to keep looking at her so I looked around the bar instead.\

I met the gaze of the biggest barman standing arms crossed by the men's washroom. His eyes were softer than I'd ever seen them, but then again we had never made eye contact before. He looked at me like he felt sorry for me. What did he know?\

Don't judge me. I was horny and she was a real women. I had a mind to steer the evening somewhere interesting.\

She agreed. Along the way she asked if we could stop and get some fresh air for a minute. It was one of those summer nights when the heat didn't die with the sun but the night breeze kept things in an alternating state of warm and cool almost akin to a natural body massage. I parked in behind a middle school.\

I got out and took my shoes off.\
\
"It's actually good to walk in grass barefoot. It's an old Tamil health trick. Natural therapy."\

Mariah came outside and leaned against the front hood. She brought her duffel bag out with her and pulled a litre bottle of whiskey out of it.\

"What the fuck," I said.\

She didn't bother to explain and poured a disposable plastic cup full of liquor.\
\

\
"You think I don't fucking know that? Everyone tells me that. Well, you all can fuck off. I know what I need and I know how to take care of myself." She took another swig.\

"You've been asking me to buy you drinks all night. It's obvious your dependant. But forget about me, you're dependant on booze and it'll ruin your life."\

And then she started crying.\

"You don't know how tough it is. My life is fucked. I don't work. My last two boyfriends left me and cheated on me. My parents disowned me. My last boyfriend beat me. You seemed different."\
\
She couldn't lie to save herself from a loaded, pointed gun. I wasn't buying any of it.\
\
I was looking for a way out and away. I remembered where we were in relation to everything. She was only few blocks from home. She'd be OK.\
\
"I'm leaving." I went for the car. She went for the passenger side but I told her she wasn't coming along.\
\
She put her duffel in the ground and started fiddling with her phone while I pressed the ignition. I still had the window open from the drive over. Mariah bent in to the car through the one that used to be hers.\
\
"Look," she turned her phone screen towards me. It was cracked square down the middle.\
\
"This guy wants to pick me up and hang out," she said.\
\
"Then call him over."\
\
I slammed the door shut and peeled out of there. She forgot her smokes in the bucket of the passenger seats. I chucked them out the window at the first red light.
